drug_class: Non-selective beta-blocker with alpha-1 blocking activity

avoid_supplements.name: Ephedra (ma huang)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Sympathomimetic effects directly antagonize beta-blocker activity; risk of hypertensive crisis and arrhythmias
avoid_supplements.action: Contraindicated; counsel patient to avoid entirely

avoid_supplements.name: Yohimbine
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Alpha-2 antagonist increases sympathetic activity, reducing carvedilol efficacy and risking blood pressure elevation

avoid_supplements.name: Licorice root (high dose)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Causes sodium retention and potassium depletion, elevates blood pressure and reduces carvedilol efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid; if used, limit to <100mg/day and monitor electrolytes and BP

caution_supplements.name: Ginseng
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have mild sympathomimetic effects that could slightly reduce beta-blocker efficacy
caution_supplements.action: Monitor blood pressure; use with caution and inform prescriber

caution_supplements.name: Hawthorn
caution_supplements.mechanism: Additive cardiac effects; may increase risk of hypotension or bradycardia
caution_supplements.action: Monitor heart rate and blood pressure; coordinate with prescriber

caution_supplements.name: Magnesium supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: May potentiate carvedilol's blood pressure-lowering effects
caution_supplements.action: Monitor BP; obtain baseline serum magnesium; avoid excessive supplementation

avoid_foods.name: High-fat meals with carvedilol dosing
avoid_foods.mechanism: Food increases carvedilol absorption variability; high-fat meals increase peak levels and bioavailability by up to 30%
avoid_foods.action: Take carvedilol consistently with or without food; avoid high-fat meals immediately before/after dosing to maintain stable levels

caution_foods.name: Potassium-rich foods (bananas, spinach, potatoes)
caution_foods.mechanism: Carvedilol may cause hyperkalemia in susceptible patients, especially with renal impairment or ACE inhibitor co-use
caution_foods.action: Monitor serum potassium levels periodically; no strict restriction needed but avoid excessive intake; counsel patient

caution_foods.name: Tyramine-rich foods (aged cheeses, cured meats, soy sauce)
caution_foods.mechanism: Theoretical risk of hypertensive response if beta-blockade is overcome; minimal clinical significance with carvedilol
caution_foods.action: No strict avoidance required; monitor for unusual BP elevation

monitoring_notes: Monitor blood pressure, heart rate, and serum electrolytes (potassium, magnesium) regularly, especially if supplements or dietary changes are introduced. Assess medication adherence and timing relative to meals to optimize carvedilol efficacy and minimize adverse effects.
